h1: API 510 Training: Online Exam Preparation for the Pressure Vessel Inspector Certification
html:
API 510 training for the pressure vessel inspector exam

The API 510 Pressure Vessel Inspector examination tests whether you can inspect, rate, repair and alter pressure vessels in service. It has 170 questions, of which 140 are scored and 30 are unscored pretest items. The first 110 are closed-book and take 2.75 hours; after a 45-minute lunch come 60 open-book questions in 3.75 hours, answered with the code PDFs on the test-centre computer. With the tutorial the day runs to 7.5 hours, sat in person at a Prometric test centre where no notes or books are allowed.

Atlantis NDT's API 510 course is preparation for that day. It is self-paced and online, so you work through it around shifts, outages and turnarounds, and an instructor answers your questions as you go. The American Petroleum Institute (API) sets the eligibility rules, runs the examination through its Individual Certification Programs (ICP) and issues the certification. You apply to API yourself, and the certificate comes only from passing API's exam.

Who the API 510 course suits, and eligibility in brief

Most candidates already work around pressure vessels: NDT technicians who have spent years taking thickness readings on columns, drums and exchangers, welding inspectors moving into in-service work, operators and maintenance supervisors, and reliability engineers who need the credential to sign inspection records.

API combines education with experience gained in the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency. A bachelor's degree in engineering or technology needs one year of supervising or performing inspection; a two-year degree or certificate needs two years of pressure vessel experience, a high school diploma three, and no formal education five or more, each including at least a year of inspection. The detail, including military service, is on the API 510 certification requirements page. Check it before you enrol, because no course can change whether API accepts your application.

The API 510 Body of Knowledge, code by code

API publishes a Body of Knowledge for each set of exam windows and a Publications Effectivity Sheet naming the edition of each document examined. The course is built on both, and you study the editions on the sheet for the window you book rather than whatever copy your plant library holds. The current API 510 Body of Knowledge draws on ten documents:

DocumentWhat the exam expects
API 510The whole code except Section 9 and Appendix E: inspection organisation, intervals, corrosion rates, remaining life, relief devices, repairs, alterations, rerating and testing after repair.
API RP 571Definitions and selected damage mechanisms, such as amine and caustic cracking, chloride cracking, CUI, brittle fracture, high-temperature hydrogen attack, sulfidation and wet H2S damage.
API RP 572Pressure vessel inspection practice: reasons, frequency, methods and records.
API RP 576Pressure-relieving devices, main text only.
API RP 577 and RP 578Welding processes, inspection and metallurgy; material verification. Both in full.
ASME Section VIII, Division 1Shell and head thickness and MAWP, joint efficiency, pressure testing, impact testing, weld sizes at openings and general NDE rules.
ASME Section VArticles 1, 2 and 6, Article 7 (yoke and prod only) and SE-797 in Article 23.
ASME Section IXWPS, PQR and welder qualification review for SMAW, GTAW, GMAW or SAW on P-No. 1, 3, 4, 5 and 8.
ASME PCC-2Selected repair articles, from insert plates and fillet-welded patches to hot taps, flange repair and NDE in lieu of a pressure test.

The Body of Knowledge also names what is out of scope, including external pressure calculations, wind and seismic loads, flanges, tubesheets and relief valve sizing, and the course does not spend your time on them. The RP 571 list is short on purpose: learn each mechanism's appearance, the materials and conditions that make equipment susceptible, and the methods that find it. For background reading, see the API 510 code explainer and the Section VIII Division 1 overview.

API 510 calculations, with worked examples

Calculations are where many candidates drop marks. Problems come in US customary and SI units, and the corrosion and interval formulas can appear in the closed-book half, so you need them memorised as well as findable. These examples use round numbers; the course works through many more.

Corrosion rate, remaining life and inspection interval

A vessel shell measured 0.750 in. when first read 14 years ago, 0.610 in. six years ago and 0.560 in. today. Its required thickness is 0.445 in. (next example).

  • Long-term rate = (0.750 − 0.560) ÷ 14 = 0.0136 in. per year; short-term rate = (0.610 − 0.560) ÷ 6 = 0.0083 in. per year.
  • Remaining corrosion allowance = 0.560 − 0.445 = 0.115 in.
  • Remaining life at the higher rate = 0.115 ÷ 0.0136 = about 8.5 years.
  • Internal or on-stream interval = the lesser of half the remaining life and 10 years: about 4.2 years. External visual = the lesser of 5 years and the internal interval: also about 4.2 years.

API 510 leaves the choice of rate to the inspector, with a corrosion specialist, as the one that best reflects current conditions; with no reason given to prefer either, take the higher. Where remaining life is under four years, the interval may be the full remaining life up to two years. The API inspection interval calculator applies the same rules.

Shell thickness and MAWP (UG-27)

Take an inside radius R of 30 in., an allowable stress S of 20,000 psi given in the problem, a joint efficiency E of 0.85 and a design pressure P of 250 psi. Under UG-27(c)(1), t = PR ÷ (SE − 0.6P) = 7,500 ÷ 16,850 = 0.445 in. Rearranged, MAWP = SEt ÷ (R + 0.6t); at today's 0.560 in. that is 9,520 ÷ 30.336 = about 314 psi. Watch whether R is taken in the corroded condition and whether a corrosion allowance is added or removed. A spherical shell under UG-27(d) uses t = PR ÷ (2SE − 0.2P).

Heads (UG-32)

For a 2:1 ellipsoidal head, UG-32(c) gives t = PD ÷ (2SE − 0.2P). With an inside diameter of 60 in., 250 psi, 20,000 psi and a seamless head qualifying for E = 1.0, t = 15,000 ÷ 39,950 = 0.375 in. A hemispherical head under UG-32(e) uses t = PL ÷ (2SE − 0.2P), with L the inside spherical radius. A favourite question gives a measured head thickness and asks whether the head still meets the code at a stated pressure: compare the measured thickness, less future corrosion, with the required thickness, or work out the head's MAWP.

Joint efficiency

Start with the weld category under UW-3 and the extent of radiography from the nameplate marking and UW-11. Table UW-12 then gives E: for a Type 1 double-welded butt joint, 1.00 with full radiography, 0.85 with spot and 0.70 with none. Seamless sections take E from UW-12(d), welded pipe from UW-12(e). Many wrong answers apply the efficiency of the wrong joint category.

Static head

With a specific gravity of 1.0, each foot of liquid adds 0.433 psi. If a bottom head sits 40 ft below the top and its part MAWP is 270 psi, the static head there is 17.3 psi, so that part limits the vessel to 252.7 psi at the top. Repeat for every part; the lowest result is the vessel MAWP (UG-98 separates the two).

Test pressure (UG-99 and UG-100)

Minimum hydrostatic test pressure is 1.3 × MAWP × LSR, the lowest ratio among the vessel's materials of allowable stress at test temperature to that at design temperature. With 250 psi MAWP, 20,000 psi at test and 17,500 psi at design temperature, LSR = 1.143 and the test is about 371 psi; a pneumatic test uses 1.1 instead, about 314 psi. The code recommends a metal temperature at least 30°F above the MDMT during a hydrotest and requires it for a pneumatic test. For when API 510 needs a test after repair, see pressure testing after repair.

Impact testing and weld size

MDMT questions follow a sequence: assign the material to its curve in Figure UCS-66, find the governing thickness, read the coldest MDMT without impact testing, then check whether UCS-66(b) allows a reduction for a lightly stressed part. UG-20(f) exempts some thin P-No. 1 materials outright, UCS-68(c) credits heat treatment that was not otherwise required, and UG-84 sets out the Charpy test. For welds at openings, the fillet throat is taken as 0.7 times the leg, so a 3/8 in. leg gives a 0.26 in. throat, and a required 0.25 in. throat needs a leg of 0.36 in. under UW-16.

Is the API 510 exam open book?

Partly. The first 110 questions are closed-book, so formulas, intervals, definitions and inspection practice have to be in your head. The last 60 are open-book, but at a Prometric centre that means PDFs of the examined documents on screen, not your own annotated copies.

Open-book technique can be learned. Decide which document a question comes from before you look: a fillet-welded patch belongs to PCC-2, a welder's bend test to Section IX, relief valve inspection to API 510 and RP 576. Look for the code's own words and paragraph numbers rather than your paraphrase, read the exceptions, and keep moving: 60 questions in 3.75 hours is under four minutes each.

How to pass the API 510 exam: a study plan in phases

The course sets no timetable, because candidates start from very different places, but it follows a sequence:

  1. Map the Body of Knowledge and effectivity sheet for your window, and note what is excluded.
  2. Learn API 510 itself, the backbone of the closed-book half.
  3. Build the calculations in both unit systems until you need no reference.
  4. Add the recommended practices: RP 571, 572, 576, 577 and 578.
  5. Section IX and Section V: practise WPS and PQR review and learn the NDE articles.
  6. PCC-2 repairs: what each listed article allows and its limits.
  7. Timed practice papers, tracing every wrong answer back to its paragraph, until scores are steady.

Most people underestimate step 3 and overestimate how far reading alone carries them. For extra material, see the free API 510 practice questions.

API 510 practice questions and practice exams

Untimed, practice questions show which parts of the Body of Knowledge you do not yet understand; timed, in papers that copy the closed-book and open-book split, they teach the pace of the day. The course questions are original and come with explanations, so a wrong answer sends you back to the code. Be wary of banks sold as "actual exam questions": API's examinations are confidential, and answers from an old effectivity sheet can be wrong for your window.

Choosing API 510 online training or a classroom course

Preparation comes as intensive seminars before an exam window, blended programmes, recorded video courses and question banks. A seminar suits someone who already knows the codes; self-paced study suits candidates who cannot leave site, work rotating shifts, or need to revisit the calculations several times. With any of them, check that the material names your window's editions, teaches the calculations step by step, lets you ask a person, and copies the real exam split. Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider, and with any provider the certificate comes only from API.

After the API 510 exam: certification and recertification

A pass leads to the API 510 Pressure Vessel Inspector certification, valid for three years and accredited by ANSI under ISO/IEC 17024. To recertify you apply from 90 days before expiry (a 90-day grace period carries late fees), show that at least 20% of your last three years went on performing or supervising pressure vessel inspection, and log 24 hours of continuing professional development across at least two categories. Every six years there is also a web quiz on code changes: 25 open-book questions in four hours, with one retake. Miss the grace period or the work requirement and you sit the full exam again.

Employer sponsorship for API 510 candidates

Owner-users and inspection contractors often sponsor several candidates ahead of a turnaround season or a contract that names API 510 inspectors. Because the course is self-paced, an experienced NDT technician and a graduate engineer each move at their own speed. Eligibility stays personal, so check each candidate's experience record before enrolling them. Fees are quoted on request for one candidate or a group. Atlantis also runs ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based UT Level II training and remote risk-based inspection studies for owners moving vessels to RBI intervals.

faq.q: Is the API 510 exam open book?
faq.a: Partly. The first 110 questions are closed-book and the last 60 open-book. In the open-book section the examined codes and recommended practices are PDFs on the test-centre computer; you cannot take your own books, notes or tabbed copies into a Prometric centre. So practise finding answers in plain PDFs against the clock, and memorise what the closed-book half needs.

faq.q: How many questions are on the API 510 exam?
faq.a: There are 170 questions: 140 scored and 30 unscored pretest items that look like the rest, so treat every question as if it counts. The day is 7.5 hours, made up of a short tutorial, 2.75 hours for 110 closed-book questions, a 45-minute lunch and 3.75 hours for 60 open-book questions, all at a designated Prometric test centre.

faq.q: Can I take API 510 training online?
faq.a: Yes. The Atlantis API 510 course is online and self-paced: you start when you enrol, study on your own schedule with no class times to attend, and send questions to an instructor when a calculation or clause will not come out. The examination itself is not online; API holds it in person at Prometric test centres, and you apply to API separately.

faq.q: What calculations are on the API 510 exam?
faq.a: From API 510: metal loss, corrosion rate, remaining corrosion allowance, remaining life and inspection interval. From Section VIII Division 1: joint efficiency, static head, thickness and MAWP of cylindrical and spherical shells and of ellipsoidal and hemispherical heads, hydrostatic and pneumatic test pressure, impact testing and MDMT exemptions, and fillet weld size at openings. External pressure, wind and seismic calculations are excluded.

faq.q: Which code editions should I study for API 510?
faq.a: Those named on the Publications Effectivity Sheet for the exam window you book. API issues a Body of Knowledge and an effectivity sheet for each set of windows, and the exam follows them, not the newest edition on the market. Check the sheet when you register, and tell the instructor if you move to a different window.

faq.q: Do I need an NDT certification to sit API 510?
faq.a: No. API looks at education and pressure vessel experience gained in the last 10 years with an authorized inspection agency, including at least one year supervising or performing inspection. Many candidates are NDT technicians, but welders, operators and engineers qualify through the same routes; see the API 510 certification requirements.

faq.q: Is Atlantis NDT an API-approved training provider?
faq.a: No. Atlantis NDT is not an API-approved, API-accredited or API-endorsed training provider, and the course does not grant any certification. It is independent exam preparation built on the Body of Knowledge API publishes. API sets the eligibility rules, administers the examination and issues the API 510 certification to candidates who pass.
